output.reason: Sudden, painless, persistent monocular vision loss described as a curtain over the right eye two hours ago requires immediate emergency assessment for central retinal artery occlusion (a stroke equivalent) or retinal detachment.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Sudden painless loss of vision in one eye that hasn't returned can signal a blocked retinal artery (a stroke-type event) or a detached retina, both needing urgent eye and stroke assessment. Do not drive yourself — have someone take you or call 911. If you develop weakness, numbness, face droop or speech trouble, call 911 immediately.
